answer: Trust-seeded random-walk ranking resists sybils: short walks launched from the honest seed spread trust like a beacon down a ridge, but reaching the sybil region means crossing the few narrow attack edges, so only a trickle of walk-probability leaks across. Rank is landing mass after few steps; a sybil cluster, however densely interlinked, shares one thin cut's mass split among all its fakes, so per-fake rank collapses as the cluster grows — a zephyr dying before the bottleneck. Precondition: attack edges are few relative to honest degree.
